DIADEMA  ARANEA.

The  Cross  Spider.  Arachnida.

A  large  spider  found  in  Europe  and  America,  its  body  ovoid,  a  longitudinal
line  on  back,  of  yellow  and  white  points,  intersected  by  three  similar  lines.  Used
as  a  remedy  by  Wm.  Gross  as  early  as  1833,  and  mentioned  in  the  older  homoeo-
pathic M'orks,  but  not  proved  until  later  by  Grauvogl,  see  his  Text  Book,  2d  edi-
tion, 1866,  and  Allen's  Encyclopedia,  vol.  4.

The  symptoms  are  mainly  based  on  clinical  experience.

The  tincture  is  prepared  by  maceration  of  the  insect  in  alcohol.

Digitalis  is  cultivated  in  gardens,  and  is  found  wild  throughout  Europe,
where  it  prefers  siliceous  soil,  generally  avoiding  limestone  districts.  This  fact
was  mentioned  by  Wm.  Lewis,  as  early  as  1768,  in  his  Materia  Medica,  where  he
remarks:  "It  is  observable  of  this  plant  that  it  grows  only  on  gravelly  soils;
rarely  or  never  on  those  where  there  are  strata  of  calcareous  earths  or  stones
underneath."

This  drug  was  extensively  proved  by  Hahnemann  and  his  provers  (See  Chro-
nische  Krankheiten,  v.  3),  as  well  as  by  later  provers.  Toxicological  reports  and
effects  on  the  sick  are  numerous,  but,  as  usual  in  our  arrangement,  symptoms
veriiied  by  cures  are  given  the  preference.

The  symptoms  of  Digitaline  and  Digitoxinum,  active  principles  of  Digitalis,
are  so  similar,  that  a  separate  classification  is  not  attempted;  of  the  latter  we  have
a  fragmentary  proving  by  Kopfe,  see  Allen's  Encyclopedia,  v.  4,  p.  121,  and  the
former  was  proved  by  Baehr  (see  Baehr's  llonograph),  whose  symptoms  are  in-
cluded, with  others  from  general  experiment  and  poisonings,  in  Allen's  arrange-
ment. Encyclopedia,  v.  4,  p.  75
